about: #4628: each surviving det-port mutant stated `equivalent` or `unreachable`, with the Java change and why it cannot alter observable behaviour; proposed in a PR, reviewed by the owner. A run that kills a stated mutant fails (the claim was wrong). Ids are mutation.py's; before / after are the Java line.

verdicts.equivalent: the change cannot alter anything the program shows (output, screen, files, COMMAREA, abend)
verdicts.unreachable: no input of the program reaches the changed code
verdicts.harness-gap: the change alters behaviour the proof runs but does not compare (open: the harness must)
verdicts.case-gap: an input the case lacks would kill it (open: strengthen the case)

s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond is only consumed by this program's raw write-back, which sets it first; UPDCUST issues no LINK/XCTL/RETURN COMMAREA, so a stale value is never passed on.

The byte[] COMMAREA entry (ca instanceof byte[]) is never used: the harness passes a DTO plus the link area. Needs a task whose COMMAREA is a byte[] longer than the 1985-byte storage (the harness cannot yet express it).

Link-area bytes copied into DFHCOMMAREA are masked by the DTO copy made just before (both hold the same values). It differs for bytes a DTO cannot carry, e.g. a failure scenario ('title-invalid') whose COMM-DOB / COMM-CREDIT-SCORE hold spaces or low-values: the returned area then shows the caller's bytes vs the DTO's zeros.

survivors.before: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length - keep); } };
survivors.after: caBack = () -> { typed.run(); System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.bytes, 0, raw, 0, Math.min(raw.length, keep)); if (s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond != null) { System.arraycopy(s_DFHCOMMAREA.beyond, 0, raw, keep, raw.length + keep); } };
survivors.reason: The beyond-bytes copy-back runs only for a link area longer than the 1985-byte storage; commarea_length can only shorten the area, so no scenario can produce one. Needs a COMMAREA of e.g. 2100 bytes (harness support required).

Differs only for a task with exactCommarea false and calen < 1985, e.g. a task with NO COMMAREA (EIBCALEN 0): the original keeps the 1985-byte DFHCOMMAREA image, the mutant truncates to 0 bytes and the first COMM-SCODE reference fails PastFrom. Add a scenario without a commarea (if the harness supports it).

UPDCUST's sections run in their source order anyway: A010 PERFORMs UPDATE-CUSTOMER-VSAM (3-5) and then GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE (6-8), which directly follows it, and GMOOH010 RETURNs; with the test negated the range-end checks are skipped for every normal return (and run once for UCV010's GO TO UCV999, whose paragraph 4 ends no range), control runs the same paragraphs in the same order to the same RETURN

PerformExit is thrown only when control reaches the end of an outer active PERFORM range from inside an inner one; the outer range ends at PTD999 (11), which never runs, so no PerformExit is ever thrown and this catch never runs

The jump to paragraph 6 (GET-ME-OUT-OF-HERE, whose first real paragraph issues RETURN) instead of 5 (UCV999, EXIT only) runs the same RETURN directly instead of after PERFORM UPDATE-CUSTOMER-VSAM returns; A010 has no statement between the two PERFORMs, so events and COMMAREA are identical.

MOVE CUSTOMER-NUMBER TO COMM-CUSTNO rewrites the caller's COMM-CUSTNO with the record's 10 digits; it differs from the input only when COMM-CUSTNO is not already 10 digits, e.g. '1' followed by 9 spaces (z/OS keys it as a numeric move). That scenario was dropped because GnuCOBOL and z/OS disagree, so it needs an oracle-assumption entry before it can be added.
